newsitem.title: HONG KONG: COSCO Hong Kong sets US$80 million loan.
newsitem.headline: COSCO Hong Kong sets US$80 million loan.

text.p: COSCO (Hong Kong) Group's US$80 million revolving credit and term loan facility has been launched into general syndication, bankers said Wednesday.
They said the facility has a final maturity of five years with an average life of four years.
The amortising loan has an availability period of 24 months. Lenders have the option of extending the availability period for an additional 12 months.
Repayment will be in six equal semi-annual instalments with a grace period of 30 months if lenders do not exercise the option to extend the availability period.
The repayment schedule will be reduced to five equal semi-annual instalments if lenders exercise that option.
The loan pays an interest margin of 111.25 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate.
Fees for co-arranger committing US$8 million or more are 20 basis points for an all-in return of 116.25 basis points.
Fees for lead managers committing US$5-7 million are 15 basis points for an all-in return of 115 basis points.
Fees for managers committing US$2-4 million are 10 basis points for an all-in return of 113.75 basis points.
Credit Lyonnais, Credit Suisse, Hypobank, Hang Seng Bank and Commerz East Asia are arrangers.
The company will use proceeds of the loan for present and future investment in the development of ports and terminals in Asia, to help finance new ships and for general working capital.
COSCO (Hong Kong) Group is wholly owned by China Ocean Shipping Group Co. COSCO Hong Kong Group owns about 56.9 percent of Hong Kong listed COSCO Pacific Ltd
